text:
maria: heads-up — seeing a spike in GPU pod evictions on cluster-us-east-1 this morning. ~40 pods restarted over the last 2h, most model-serving.

maria: sample from kubelet logs:
```
I0218 09:12:34.123456 1 eviction_manager.go:558] eviction manager: pod x-model-abc evicted: node allocatable memory shortage: requested 15360Mi, available 8192Mi
```

maria: nodes are mixed sizes (v100-16g, a100-40g, some old p4-8g). Autoscaler scaled up several p4s during CI load and now we have a bunch of small leftover nodes. Pods request 1 GPU + 20Gi mem. Seems like packing mismatch.

dan: +1 saw related alerts in grafana — GPU utilization low on several nodes but pods fail to fit because of memory/GPU pairing. This is classic "scatter, then leftover" effect.

alex: do we have affinity/anti-affinity rules? a lot of our model-serving deployments use nodeSelector: gpu-type: generic and no topologySpread. That lets scheduler spread them. Might be okay for availability but terrible for tight GPU binpacking.

vinay: We started requesting cuda-mem 18Gi for some models after a memory regression last month — requests are large and hard to consolidate. For p4 (8Gi) those pods simply can't fit, causing evictions when CA replaces nodes.

maria: question: should we change scheduler behavior to prefer consolidation on larger GPU nodes, or relax requests? Concerned about making latency worse if we increase co-location.

alex: options: 1) add topologySpreadConstraints to prefer filling nodes, 2) use nodeAffinity to prefer high-memory GPU nodes for heavy models, 3) run a periodic descheduler job to move small/low-priority jobs off big nodes.

dan: another lever — add a binpack policy on our custom scheduler plugin so it scores nodes by free GPU memory first, then CPU. That reduces fragmentation but could increase blast radius on node failure.

maria: cost angle: running lots of small p4s is cheap per-hour but wastes reserved GPU memory. Consolidating onto fewer a100-40g would lower node count but increases per-node $; need an estimate.

vinay: rough calc: 10 p4-8g @ $0.60/hr vs 2 a100-40g @ $2.8/hr — switching would cut networking overhead and idle GPU waste. But migration risk for latency-critical jobs.

alex: also seeing evictions tied to taint:NoSchedule from kubelet when memory pressure happens. Pods without tolerations get evicted first which is ok, but our restart backoff is slow for grpc-serving clients. Can tweak pod disruption budgets or use preStop hooks to gracefully drain.

maria: can we get a quick experiment: 1) add preferredDuringScheduling affinity to mark a100 nodes for requests >24Gi, 2) run descheduler on a 1-hour cadence to consolidate low-priority pods, 3) temporarily set tolerant pod for evict-priority=low? who can implement?

dan: I can do the affinity + descheduler cronjob. Will create a small helm patch and run in dev first.

vinay: I'll audit model resource requests and lower some memory requests where safe, and identify models that must stay isolated.

alex: I'll add a Grafana panel showing fragmentation metric: fraction of nodes with <25% GPU utilization but >0 allocated GPUs. That should show before/after.

sre-bot: alert: cluster-us-east-1: node/p4-8g-12 terminated by autoscaler at 09:11:02 (scale-down) — 11 pods evicted.

maria: perfect, dan/vinay/alex — let's sync after the dev run. If consolidation reduces evictions we can roll to prod next week. Also we should document the tradeoffs in infra runbook (latency vs cost vs fragmentation).

dan: noted. PR coming with affinity patch and descheduler job. Will tag you all. :white_check_mark:

vinay: thanks — will post list of changed resource requests when done.

alex: also adding a short KEP-style note about optional binpacking scoring so we don't forget architecture rationale.

maria: thanks team. if we still see evictions after this, we should consider a pool with homogeneous big-GPU nodes and automated scale-down cooldowns to avoid churning small nodes.

maria: end.
